newsitem.title: GERMANY: Germany's Schaeuble ready to talk on petrol tax.
newsitem.headline: Germany's Schaeuble ready to talk on petrol tax.

text.p: Bonn is ready to discuss with opposition politicians the possibility of using taxes on petrol to secure agreement on its planned tax reform, a senior government member said on Wednesday.

"We are fully ready to talk about a petrol tax-financed cut in employment insurance contributions," Wolfgang Schaeuble, parliamentary leader of the Christian Democrats (CDU), said in a newspaper interview.
Opposition demands that non-wage labour costs be reduced as part of Bonn's tax reform was one of the sticking points in cross-party talks that finally collapsed last month.

Schaeble, quoted in a summary of an interview to appear in Thursday's edition of the Sueddeutsche Zeitung, said he was still confident that a deal could be reached in a second mediation phase planned for this autumn.
Bonn sees the tax reform, which would reduce Germany's tax bill by around 30 billion marks, as vital to economic growth and its future competitiveness.
Previous suggestions that petrol taxes be raised have met with fierce criticism from those who argue it would damage the car industry, one of Germany's largest employers.
